---
title: "Builder Practice Exam"
---

These 72 questions cover what every Foundry builder should know: the six builder axes, taught in
the MSB 341 Product Management book. They follow the same plan as the Builder Final, which is both
the MSB 341 final and the AI Foundry entrance exam: the same six axes in the same proportions, and
an even mix of three kinds of question.

- **Know it:** what a thing is, or what it is for.
- **Use it:** a short situation; pick the tool, step, or method that fits.
- **Predict it:** what happens next, or what went wrong, and why.

No question here appears on the final. Your answers stay in this browser and are not sent to
anyone. Check one question at a time, or answer them all and score the whole exam. Every question
links to the section of the [Product Management book](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/) it comes from, so a missed question
tells you exactly what to read.

The final gives 2 hours for 84 questions. To practice at that pace, allow about 85 minutes.

A delayed retry with a cap respects the limit; retrying at once in a loop keeps failing and, on a paid service, costs money on every call.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/08-data-and-apis.html#requests-are-contracts-that-fail", "text": "Requests and How They Fail", "chapter": "Data and APIs"}]}, {"n": 28, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Hannah&#x27;s orders page filters by customer_id. It loaded instantly in September; now, with two million orders, it takes several seconds. The query has not changed. What should she check first?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Whether the query should use a LEFT JOIN"], ["B", "Whether the WHERE filter should be removed"], ["C", "Whether the page needs a larger LIMIT"], ["D", "Whether customer_id has an index"]], "answer": "D", "why": "Without an index the database reads every row to find one customer's orders, which slows as the table grows. An index on customer_id lets it jump to the matching rows.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/08-data-and-apis.html#asking-the-database-a-question", "text": "Asking the Database a Question", "chapter": "Data and APIs"}]}, {"n": 29, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Diego wants a Suggest Title button that asks Claude for a title. Where should the call to the model API happen?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "In the button's component, with the key in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable"], ["B", "In the browser, with the key saved in the user's local storage"], ["C", "In a server route, with the key in a server-only variable"], ["D", "In the browser, through Supabase with the publishable key"]], "answer": "C", "why": "A model call needs a secret key and costs money, so it runs in a route handler on the server, which reads the key from an environment variable, and the button calls that route. Anything in browser code is readable by every visitor.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#where-the-call-lives", "text": "Where the Call Lives", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 30, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Jordan&#x27;s new weekly-digest screen is deployed. He wants 20 named beta users to see it in production this week, then everyone next week, with no new deploy. What should he use?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "A staging site that the beta users sign in to"], ["B", "An environment variable that turns the screen on"], ["C", "A preview URL from the branch, sent to the beta users"], ["D", "A feature flag kept in a database table of users"]], "answer": "D", "why": "A flag stored in a table is read on each request, so it can be on for 20 users and then for everyone by editing rows, with no deploy. An environment variable is on or off for a whole environment and needs a redeploy to change.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/09-version-control-testing-and-tech-debt.html#feature-flags-one-deploy-and-a-setting-for-who-sees-it", "text": "Feature flags: one deploy, and a setting for who sees it", "chapter": "Version Control, Environments, and Deploys"}]}, {"n": 31, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Maya&#x27;s app works on her laptop under npm run dev. What explains the difference?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Vercel uses a stricter TypeScript version than her laptop"], ["B", "A key in her .env.local was never added to Vercel"], ["C", "Type errors appear only once real users open a page"], ["D", "The build stops on type errors the dev server let pass"]], "answer": "D", "why": "npm run build, which Vercel runs, compiles the whole app at once and stops on a type error even when every page worked in the development server. Running npm run build on her laptop before pushing would show the same error.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/09-version-control-testing-and-tech-debt.html#the-three-environments-you-already-have", "text": "The three environments you already have", "chapter": "Version Control, Environments, and Deploys"}]}, {"n": 32, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Two months ago Lin committed an Anthropic API key in a source file to her public repo. Last week she deleted the line and pushed. Today her bill shows thousands of calls she did not make. Why?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Vercel kept serving an old build that still held the key"], ["B", "Someone guessed the key from the part the dashboard shows"], ["C", "The key is still in the history, and it still works"], ["D", "The push with the deletion never reached GitHub"]], "answer": "C", "why": "Deleting a line leaves it in every earlier commit, which anyone can read in a public repo, and the key works until it is revoked. The fix is to create a new key, revoke the old one, and keep keys in environment variables that git ignores.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/08-data-and-apis.html#secrets-and-sensitive-data", "text": "Secrets and Sensitive Data", "chapter": "Data and APIs"}]}, {"n": 33, "axis": "Application Architecture", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Lin&#x27;s ticket page checks the promo code in browser code, works out the price, and sends { price: 12 } to her server, which charges that amount. What can a user do?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Nothing, because the connection to the server is encrypted"], ["B", "Pay any price they like by editing the request"], ["C", "Only see the price, since changing it needs Lin's password"], ["D", "Nothing, because browser code is compiled before it ships"]], "answer": "B", "why": "Everything in the browser, including the requests it sends, belongs to the user, so a price worked out there can be changed. It takes the user id from the request body, which the browser fills in, and returns that user&#x27;s notes. Row-level security is on. What can a signed-in user do?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Read only their own notes, because row-level security is on"], ["B", "Read anyone's notes, by changing the id they send"], ["C", "Read nothing, because the secret key is refused from servers"], ["D", "Read others' notes, but only by stealing the secret key"]], "answer": "B", "why": "The secret key skips row-level security, so the route returns notes for whatever id the browser sends, and the user controls the browser. The route should take the user from the verified token, or query with the user's token so the policies apply.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/07-anatomy-of-an-application.html#three-credentials-publishable-key-token-secret-key", "text": "Three credentials: publishable key, token, secret key", "chapter": "Anatomy of an Application"}]}, {"n": 35, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>What counts toward a model&#x27;s context window in one call?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Only the newest message the user typed"], ["B", "Instructions, documents, the chat so far, its reply"], ["C", "Every past chat the user has had with the app"], ["D", "All of the text the model was shown during its training"]], "answer": "B", "why": "The context window holds everything sent in one call plus the answer the model writes, all counted in tokens. The smallest suit simple, high-volume work where speed matters.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#what-it-costs", "text": "What It Costs", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 38, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>In a RAG system, what is a chunk?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "One complete document, such as a whole manual"], ["B", "A single token taken from a document"], ["C", "A passage of a few hundred tokens from a document"], ["D", "The list of numbers that stands for a passage's meaning"]], "answer": "C", "why": "Documents are split into passages of a few hundred tokens, and each passage is the unit that gets embedded, stored, and retrieved. How many output tokens will it use per day?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "400,000"], ["B", "2,000"], ["C", "12 million"], ["D", "2 million"]], "answer": "D", "why": "Output tokens per call times calls per user per day times users: 400 x 5 x 1,000 = 2 million. Multiply by the output price, and do the same for the 10 million input tokens, before shipping.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#what-it-costs", "text": "What It Costs", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 40, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Jordan&#x27;s app reads customer emails, has a model pull out the refund amount, and issues the refund. A wrong amount costs real money. Which check belongs in the path?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Ask the model to double-check its own answer first"], ["B", "Set the temperature to 0 for this one call"], ["C", "Compare the amount with the order record before paying"], ["D", "Pay only when the model says it is confident in the amount"]], "answer": "C", "why": "Where a wrong answer is expensive, the check sits in the path and uses something trusted, here the order record or a person approving. The model's own review and confidence come from the same process that made the error.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#where-it-breaks", "text": "Where It Breaks", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 41, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Priya wants a model&#x27;s honest view of her pricing plan before she shows it to investors. Which request is most likely to surface real problems?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Ask whether it agrees the plan is strong"], ["B", "Ask it for the strongest case against the plan"], ["C", "Tell it she is confident, then ask for a rating"], ["D", "Ask the same question again until two answers match"]], "answer": "B", "why": "Training on human ratings taught models to lean toward agreement, so a leading question tends to get a yes. Asking for the case against works against that lean, and she can then judge each point on the evidence.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/10-how-models-work.html#step-6-fine-tuning-and-human-feedback-shape-behavior", "text": "Step 6: Fine-tuning and human feedback shape behavior", "chapter": "How Models Work"}]}, {"n": 42, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>A help center searches its articles by embedding. A user types &quot;I can&#x27;t get into my account.&quot; Which article will most likely rank first?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Understanding your monthly account statement"], ["B", "None, since no article contains that exact phrase"], ["C", "Whichever article is newest or most viewed"], ["D", "Resetting a forgotten password"]], "answer": "D", "why": "Embeddings place text by meaning, so a complaint about getting in sits near the password reset article though they share almost no words. The statement article shares the word \"account\" but means something else.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/10-how-models-work.html#step-2-tokens-become-embeddings", "text": "Step 2: Tokens become embeddings", "chapter": "How Models Work"}]}, {"n": 43, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Lin&#x27;s app asks a model, with default settings, for an email subject line. She sends the identical request in five separate calls. What should she expect?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "The same subject line all five times"], ["B", "Subject lines that differ from call to call"], ["C", "Different lines, because the model learns after each call"], ["D", "Different lines, because it avoids repeating past answers"]], "answer": "B", "why": "Each next token is drawn from probabilities, so the same input can give a different line each time, and one different early token changes the rest. The five calls share nothing with each other.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/10-how-models-work.html#step-4-the-model-predicts-the-next-token", "text": "Step 4: The model predicts the next token", "chapter": "How Models Work"}]}, {"n": 44, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Maya trains a model to flag spam using 50,000 emails, each paired with a label. After training, what will the model most likely do with a new newsletter?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Spot the bad labels during training and ignore them"], ["B", "Mark it as not spam, since newsletters are wanted mail"], ["C", "Refuse to classify it until the labels are fixed"], ["D", "Flag it as spam, as its labels taught it"]], "answer": "D", "why": "Training adjusts the parameters until the predictions match the labels it is given, right or wrong, so the model learns the mistake. Nothing in training checks whether a label is true.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/10-how-models-work.html#ai-and-machine-learning", "text": "AI and Machine Learning", "chapter": "How Models Work"}]}, {"n": 45, "axis": "AI Systems", "type": "Predict it", "stem": "<p>Sam&#x27;s bot answers from uploaded product manuals. A missing document produces a confident wrong answer, which is why retrieval is tested on its own.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#grounding-answers-in-your-data", "text": "Grounding Answers in Your Data", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 46, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>In plan mode, what does Claude Code hold back until you approve the plan?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Edits to your project's files"], ["B", "Reading the files in your project"], ["C", "Asking you clarifying questions"], ["D", "Running commands that look around"]], "answer": "A", "why": "In plan mode Claude reads, searches, runs exploring commands, and asks questions, but it does not edit your files until you approve the plan.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/06b-specs.html#claude-codes-plan-mode", "text": "Claude Code's plan mode", "chapter": "Specs: Designing the Build"}, {"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#the-controls-from-tightest-to-loosest", "text": "The controls, from tightest to loosest", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 47, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>In auto mode, what decides whether Claude&#x27;s next action runs without asking you?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "The commands listed in your CLAUDE.md."], ["B", "Claude's own judgment about the task."], ["C", "A second model that reviews each action first."], ["D", "Nothing; every action runs in auto mode."]], "answer": "C", "why": "Auto mode hands the approval to a separate model, a classifier, that reviews each action before it runs and blocks risky ones, such as actions beyond what you asked for.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#the-controls-from-tightest-to-loosest", "text": "The controls, from tightest to loosest", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 48, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>What is the difference between a CLAUDE.md instruction and a permission rule?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "The instruction covers all projects; the rule covers one"], ["B", "The instruction is advice; the rule is always checked"], ["C", "The instruction blocks commands; the rule only warns"], ["D", "The instruction loads once; the rule loads every turn"]], "answer": "B", "why": "The model weighs a CLAUDE.md instruction against everything else it reads, so a message can talk past it. Claude Code checks a permission rule on every tool call, whatever the model decides.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#advice-versus-enforcement", "text": "Advice Versus Enforcement", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 49, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>What belongs in a project&#x27;s CLAUDE.md?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Decisions and traps the code does not show"], ["B", "A list of every file and what it contains"], ["C", "A copy of yesterday's conversation with Claude"], ["D", "Long procedures used once a month"]], "answer": "A", "why": "CLAUDE.md is read in every session, so it should hold what the agent cannot work out by reading the code: decisions, constraints, and traps. Occasional procedures belong in a skill.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#claude.md-your-projects-memory", "text": "CLAUDE.md: your project's memory", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 50, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>What is indirect prompt injection?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "A user typing a very long question"], ["B", "A model making up a confident wrong answer"], ["C", "Instructions hidden in content it reads"], ["D", "A request blocked for exceeding the rate limit"]], "answer": "C", "why": "Indirect prompt injection is an attack that arrives through data the model reads, such as a web page, a ticket, or a PDF, carrying instructions that try to steer it.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#where-it-breaks", "text": "Where It Breaks", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 51, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Know it", "stem": "<p>Which action can neither /rewind nor git on your laptop undo?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Claude editing a file with its edit tool"], ["B", "Deleting a committed file with rm"], ["C", "A script sending emails to your users"], ["D", "Renaming a committed file with mv"]], "answer": "C", "why": "An email that has been sent has left your laptop, so nothing on the laptop can recall it. /rewind covers Claude's edits, and git restores committed files.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#what-can-be-undone", "text": "What can be undone", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}, {"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#blast-radius", "text": "Blast Radius", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 52, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Maya wants Claude Code to list the open issues in her GitHub repository and summarize them. What is the simplest way for Claude to get the issues?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Run gh issue list in the terminal."], ["B", "Add a GitHub MCP server, then use its tools."], ["C", "Paste the issues into the chat from the website."], ["D", "Write a script that calls GitHub's API with a new key."]], "answer": "A", "why": "A command-line tool that is already installed and signed in is the shortest route: Claude can run it at once with Maya's login. Which test cases should she use?<\/p>", "options": [["A", "Ten recipes she writes to cover cases she expects"], ["B", "Recipes the model labels, used as the answers"], ["C", "Real user recipes, labeled by a person"], ["D", "A few recipes she checks by eye after each change"]], "answer": "C", "why": "An eval uses real inputs with expected answers a person decided before the run. Invented inputs miss the odd cases users send, and the model's own labels cannot check the model.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html#evals-knowing-whether-it-works", "text": "Evals: Knowing Whether It Works", "chapter": "Models in Your Product"}]}, {"n": 54, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Claude changed Priya&#x27;s sign-up form so it saves each person&#x27;s phone number to the database. Use the feature as a user would and confirm the result.", "read": [{"url": "https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/02-directing-the-agent.html#done-means-you-saw-it-work", "text": "Done Means You Saw It Work", "chapter": "Directing the Agent"}]}, {"n": 55, "axis": "Agentic Workflow", "type": "Use it", "stem": "<p>Lin&#x27;s research feature lets a model call a web-search tool repeatedly until it decides it has enough to answer. const KEY = "foundry-practice-final-v1";
const BANDS = [[80,"Strong"],[50,"Proficient"],[0,"Developing"]];
let st = {a:{}, c:{}};
try { st = Object.assign(st, JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || "{}")); } catch(e) {}
const save = () => { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(st)); } catch(e) {} };
const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({"&":"&amp;","<":"&lt;",">":"&gt;",'"':"&quot;"}[c]));
const band = p => BANDS.find(b => p >= b[0])[1];
const box = document.getElementById("pf-qs");

let html = "", last = "";
for (const q of Q) {
  if (q.axis !== last) { html += `<div class="pf-axis" id="axis-${q.axis.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g,"-")}">${esc(q.axis)}</div>`; last = q.axis; }
  html += `<div class="pf-q" id="q${q.n}"><div class="pf-meta"><span>Question ${q.n}</span><span class="pf-tag">${q.type}</span></div>
    <div class="pf-stem">${q.stem}</div>` +
    q.options.map(([k,v]) => `<label class="pf-opt" data-k="${k}"><input type="radio" name="q${q.n}" value="${k}"><b>${k}.</b><span>${esc(v)}</span></label>`).join("") +
    `<div class="pf-act"><button type="button" class="sec pf-check" data-n="${q.n}" disabled>Check answer</button></div><div class="pf-fbw"></div></div>`;
}
box.innerHTML = html;

function feedback(q) {
  const el = document.getElementById("q" + q.n), pick = st.a[q.n], right = pick === q.answer;
  el.classList.toggle("ok", right); el.classList.toggle("bad", !right);
  el.querySelectorAll(".pf-opt").forEach(o => {
    o.classList.toggle("right", o.dataset.k === q.answer);
    o.classList.toggle("wrong", o.dataset.k === pick && !right);
  });
  const reads = q.read.map(r => `<li><a href="${r.url}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">${esc(r.text)}</a> <span style="color:#555">(${esc(r.chapter)})</span></li>`).join("");
  el.querySelector(".pf-fbw").innerHTML = `<div class="pf-fb"><span class="v">${right ? "Correct." : `Not quite. The answer is ${q.answer}.`}</span> ${esc(q.why)}
    <div style="margin-top:6px">Read in the Product Management book:</div><ul>${reads}</ul></div>`;
  const b = el.querySelector(".pf-check"); b.textContent = "Checked"; b.disabled = true;
}
function clearFb(q) {
  const el = document.getElementById("q" + q.n);
  el.classList.remove("ok","bad");
  el.querySelectorAll(".pf-opt").forEach(o => o.classList.remove("right","wrong"));
  el.querySelector(".pf-fbw").innerHTML = "";
  const b = el.querySelector(".pf-check"); b.textContent = "Check answer"; b.disabled = !st.a[q.n];
}
function progress() {
  const n = Object.keys(st.a).length;
  document.getElementById("pf-count").textContent = `${n} of ${Q.length} answered`;
  document.getElementById("pf-fill").style.width = (100 * n / Q.length) + "%";
}
function score(scroll) {
  const axes = {}; let got = 0;
  for (const q of Q) {
    const a = axes[q.axis] || (axes[q.axis] = {n:0, r:0, ans:0});
    a.n++; if (st.a[q.n]) a.ans++;
    if (st.a[q.n] === q.answer) { a.r++; got++; }
    if (st.a[q.n]) { st.c[q.n] = 1; feedback(q); }
  }
  save();
  const pct = Math.round(100 * got / Q.length);
  const rows = Object.entries(axes).map(([ax,a]) => { const p = Math.round(100*a.r/a.n);
    return `<tr><td><a href="#axis-${ax.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g,"-")}">${esc(ax)}</a></td><td class="n">${a.r} of ${a.n}</td><td class="n">${p}%</td><td class="pf-band ${band(p)}">${band(p)}</td></tr>`; }).join("");
  const missed = Q.filter(q => st.a[q.n] !== q.answer);
  const unanswered = Q.length - Object.keys(st.a).length;
  const list = missed.map(q => `<li><a href="#q${q.n}">Question ${q.n}</a> (${esc(q.axis)}): read <a href="${q.read[0].url}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">${esc(q.read[0].text)}</a></li>`).join("");
  document.getElementById("pf-res").innerHTML = `<div class="pf-res"><h3>${got} of ${Q.length} correct (${pct}%)</h3>
    <div>${unanswered ? `${unanswered} unanswered, counted as missed. ` : ""}On the final, each axis is reported as Developing (below 50%), Proficient (50 to 79%) or Strong (80% and up).</div>
    <table><thead><tr><th>Axis</th><th class="n">Correct</th><th class="n">Percent</th><th>Band</th></tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table>
    ${missed.length ? `<details><summary>What to read: ${missed.length} question${missed.length>1?"s":""} missed or unanswered</summary><ol>${list}</ol></details>` : "<div>Every question correct.</div>"}</div>`;
  if (scroll) document.getElementById("pf-res").scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"});
}

box.addEventListener("change", e => {
  if (e.target.type !== "radio") return;
  const n = +e.target.name.slice(1); st.a[n] = e.target.value; delete st.c[n]; save();
  clearFb(Q[n-1]); progress();
});
box.addEventListener("click", e => {
  const b = e.target.closest(".pf-check"); if (!b || b.disabled) return;
  const n = +b.dataset.n; st.c[n] = 1; save(); feedback(Q[n-1]);
});
document.getElementById("pf-score").addEventListener("click", () => score(true));
document.getElementById("pf-reset").addEventListener("click", () => {
  st = {a:{}, c:{}}; save();
  document.querySelectorAll("#pf input[type=radio]").forEach(r => r.checked = false);
  Q.forEach(clearFb); document.getElementById("pf-res").innerHTML = ""; progress();
  window.scrollTo({top: document.getElementById("pf").offsetTop - 80, behavior:"smooth"});
});

for (const q of Q) {
  const k = st.a[q.n]; if (!k) continue;
  const r = document.querySelector(`input[name=q${q.n}][value=${k}]`); if (r) r.checked = true;
  clearFb(q); if (st.c[q.n]) feedback(q);
}
progress();
})();
</script>
